# GPU Profiling & NCCL Debugging

## Tools

```
NVML (NVIDIA Management Library):
  Metrics: GPU temp, power, utilization, clock speed
  Usage: real-time monitoring
  
NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communications Library):
  Debugging: all-reduce latency, bandwidth, ring topology
  Trace: event log per GPU
  
Nsight Systems:
  Profiling: CPU + GPU timeline
  Bottleneck: compute vs memory vs synchronization
  
CUDA Compute Sanitizer:
  Correctness: race conditions, memory errors
  
Torch Profiler (PyTorch):
  Integration: seamless with training code
  Trace: CPU ops, CUDA kernel time
```

---

## Key Metrics

```
Utilization (NVML "GPU util"):
  - Share of time a kernel was running; it is NOT
    SM occupancy or a measure of useful work
  - Low: GPU idle, the bottleneck is upstream
  - High: necessary, not sufficient (the work may be
    memory-bound, or an NCCL kernel may be spinning)
  - Measure: nvidia-smi, or NVML in code

Memory:
  - Used: working set size
  - Bandwidth: achieved bytes/sec vs the datasheet
    peak for YOUR GPU (it varies by SKU)
    └─ Near peak bandwidth: memory-bound
    └─ Near peak FLOP/s: compute-bound
    └─ Near neither: latency, launch, or sync bound

Clock Speed:
  - Thermal throttling: read the throttle reasons
    (thermal, power cap) instead of guessing from
    a temperature; thresholds differ by SKU
  - Power limit: hitting the cap lowers clocks

NCCL Bandwidth:
  - Ring topology: each step is limited by the
    slowest link in the ring
  - Trace: see which rank (GPU) is slow
```

---

## Bottleneck Detection

```
Training slower than expected?
          │
          ▼
  GPU util low? ──yes──► input pipeline / CPU bound
          │ no           (profile DataLoader time)
          ▼
  AllReduce slow vs ──yes──► comms: topology, NIC
  nccl-tests baseline?       binding, straggler rank
          │ no
          ▼
  Kernels slow? ──yes──► per-kernel view (nsys,
          │ no            Nsight Compute): small
          ▼               kernels, no mixed precision
  Memory growing / OOM? ──► memory snapshot
```

```
Check 1: GPU idle?
  nvidia-smi shows low utilization
  → CPU bottleneck (data loading, preprocessing)
  → Solution: async data pipeline, prefetch batches

Check 2: Data loading time?
  Torch profiler: DataLoader time >> model step time
  (hypothetical: 30s vs 5s per batch)
  → CPU is slow feeding data
  → Solution: more num_workers, local SSD, not NFS

Check 3: GPU memory error?
  CUDA OOM after N iterations
  → Memory growth: tensors kept alive (e.g. storing
    loss without .item()), or fragmentation
  → Solution: torch.cuda.memory_summary() or a memory
    snapshot to find what holds memory
    (Compute Sanitizer finds invalid accesses and
    leaked cudaMalloc, not Python-side tensor growth)

Check 4: NCCL all-reduce slow?
  Profiler: all-reduce far above the nccl-tests
  baseline on the same hardware
  → Topology issue (rank on the wrong NIC, bad route)
  → Solution: check ring topology, bind to right NIC

Check 5: Compute slow?
  Utilization high, but step time is high
  → Inefficient kernels: tiny kernels, no mixed
    precision, memory-bound ops, host syncs
  → Solution: per-kernel profile (nsys, Nsight Compute)
  (NaN/Inf loss is a correctness bug, not a speed one)
```

---

## NCCL Ring Topology

```
Scenario: 8 GPUs on 2 nodes (4 GPUs each)

Bad ring (alternates nodes: 8 network hops):
  0 → 4 → 1 → 5 → 2 → 6 → 3 → 7 → 0

Good ring (locality-aware: 2 network hops):

  node0:  0 → 1 → 2 → 3
          ▲           │ network
          │           ▼
  node1:  7 ← 6 ← 5 ← 4
```

NCCL discovers topology and builds rings itself; a bad ring usually comes from misconfiguration (wrong rank-to-GPU mapping, wrong NIC, blocked P2P).

```bash
# Detect: see the rings and channels NCCL chose
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,GRAPH \
  python train.py 2>&1 | grep -iE "ring|channel"

# Measure: run nccl-tests on the same nodes
./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 1G -f 2 -g 1
# If a cross-node link is slow: check NIC binding and routing
```

---

## Code Example

```python
import os
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from torch.profiler import profile, record_function, ProfilerActivity

# NCCL_DEBUG must be set BEFORE the process group is created
os.environ["NCCL_DEBUG"] = "INFO"
dist.init_process_group("nccl")

with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA],
             record_shapes=True, profile_memory=True) as prof:
    with record_function("model_inference"):
        model_output = model(input_tensor)

print(prof.key_averages().table(
    sort_by="self_cuda_memory_usage", row_limit=10))
# Shows which ops use the most CUDA memory

print(f"GPU 0 memory: {torch.cuda.memory_allocated(0) / 1e9:.2f} GB")

# Ring/channel setup is logged on the first collective
dist.all_reduce(tensor)
```

## Interview Checklist

- [ ] NVML vs NCCL vs nsys profilers
- [ ] Utilization vs compute vs memory-bound
- [ ] Thermal throttling detection
- [ ] NCCL ring topology and cross-network hops
- [ ] Bottleneck diagnosis (GPU idle, memory, NCCL)
- [ ] Data loading as bottleneck
- [ ] CUDA memory leaks

## Common Wrong Answers

- ❌ "High GPU utilization = good" — could still be memory-bound
- ❌ "More workers = faster data" — depends on storage (NFS bottleneck)
- ❌ "Ignore NCCL ring" — a bad topology can slow all-reduce substantially
- ❌ "Thermal throttling doesn't matter" — in synchronous training one throttled GPU slows every rank
